features.name: security automation leverage
features.description: Assesses whether the letter frames the role as using software to multiply security capacity rather than merely doing security-adjacent development.

levels.descriptor: Shows general interest in security or backend work but does not frame the role in terms of leverage, capacity, or automation.
Mentions automation or reducing manual work in passing, but the idea is not central to the letter.
Clearly presents the role as reducing toil or scaling vulnerability handling through systems and tooling.
Builds the letter around a sharp thesis about multiplying scarce security expertise, increasing organizational capacity, or making response routine instead of heroic.

features.name: job-specific responsibility mapping
features.description: Assesses how precisely the letter connects the applicant's experience to the actual duties in the posting.

levels.descriptor: Makes broad fit claims without tying experience to the posted responsibilities.
References one relevant theme or keyword from the posting, such as security, AI, or Go.
Maps prior work to several listed duties, such as vulnerability triage, assessments, Go back-end work, or Python automation.
Closely mirrors multiple core responsibilities, including distinctive duties like variant analysis, vulnerability handling workflows, or assisting developer teams through the development lifecycle.

features.evidence: helping busy developer teams do the secure thing by default
features.name: developer enablement orientation
features.description: Captures whether the letter treats internal developers as users to be helped through safer defaults and lower-friction tooling.

levels.descriptor: Does not mention developer teams as users or beneficiaries of the work.
Suggests security helps others in general terms but without an internal-customer mindset.
Explicitly emphasizes making secure behavior easy, proactive, or default for developers.
Repeatedly frames success as removing friction for engineers and embedding security into everyday development rather than policing from the side.

features.name: foundational platform orientation
features.description: Captures attraction to core infrastructure work whose effects compound across many products or teams.

levels.descriptor: Does not express interest in platform, Core, or foundation-layer work.
Mentions large scale or broad impact in generic terms.
Explicitly says they want foundation-layer or central infrastructure work with organization-wide leverage.
Makes inherited downstream impact a core motivation and explains why platform responsibility is especially appealing.

features.name: professional software tenure
features.description: Scores the amount of post-degree software engineering experience explicitly claimed.

levels.descriptor: Limited professional tenure, roughly just above the minimum bar for the role.
Solid midlevel tenure, roughly around four to five years.
Extensive tenure for this pool, roughly six or more years.

features.name: production service scope
features.description: Assesses the breadth of concrete production-service ownership the letter claims.

levels.descriptor: Ownership is described over a small number of production services or a narrow scope.
Shows responsibility across several production services with meaningful launch or maintenance experience.
Shows broad production breadth, such as many services or repeated launch, maintenance, and testing responsibility.

features.name: academic credential level
features.description: Scores the highest formal academic training level presented in the letter.

levels.descriptor: Bachelor's degree or equivalent is the highest credential mentioned.
Master's degree is the highest credential mentioned.
Doctoral degree is the highest credential mentioned.

features.name: Python depth
features.description: Assesses how deeply the letter establishes Python as a serious working language for services, automation, or tooling.

levels.descriptor: Does not mention Python.
Mentions Python competence or occasional use without much depth.
Shows regular Python use for tooling, automation, internal services, or prototypes.
Presents Python as a central, production-grade language used across multiple contexts with clear ownership or dependency from teammates.

features.evidence: evaluation scaffolding required to deploy them responsibly
features.name: AI production rigor
features.description: Assesses the depth of applied AI experience, especially whether the letter shows operational rigor rather than merely novelty.

levels.descriptor: Does not mention AI experience.
Mentions AI or LLM work at a feature level without discussing deployment challenges.
Says they shipped model-backed functionality and addressed reliability, hardening, or predictable behavior in production.
Shows production AI maturity through language about evaluation, failure modes, trustworthiness, or disciplined deployment practices.

features.name: agentic tooling design
features.description: Assesses experience designing agent-based systems rather than only using AI APIs.

levels.descriptor: Does not describe agentic tooling.
Mentions autonomous agents at a high level but gives little architectural detail.
Describes an architecture that combines Python agents with Go back-end services.
Shows controlled agent design with bounded tasks, guardrails, permissions, logging, auditability, or similarly explicit constraints.

features.name: security assessment depth
features.description: Captures how concretely the letter demonstrates the ability to perform security assessments.

levels.descriptor: Does not mention security assessment work.
References reviews or security fundamentals in general terms without much process detail.
Clearly cites work such as threat modeling, code review, findings, remediation, or assessments of existing services.
Frames assessments as disciplined engineering work with a clear method, builder's eye, or attacker-oriented analysis.

features.name: vulnerability triage automation
features.description: Assesses direct experience automating intake and handling of vulnerability reports or findings.

levels.descriptor: Does not mention automation of vulnerability intake or triage.
Mentions security automation but not the report-flow details of triage work.
Provides a clear example of automating classification, routing, deduplication, or similar steps in vulnerability handling.
Shows substantial triage ownership and impact, such as turning a manual queue into a largely self-serve or materially lower-toil pipeline.

features.evidence: turned a brute-force correlation job into a streaming computation
features.name: algorithmic problem solving evidence
features.description: Captures whether the letter substantiates data-structures-or-algorithms strength with concrete technical problem solving.

levels.descriptor: Provides no evidence of algorithmic or data-structure work.
Claims strong algorithmic ability but leaves it abstract.
Gives one concrete redesign, optimization, or structure-choice example.
Gives a strong example that clearly changed tractability, throughput, simplicity, or system behavior in a meaningful way.

features.evidence: maintainer of an open-source tooling project
features.name: open-source ownership
features.description: Assesses how much ongoing responsibility the applicant claims in public codebases.

levels.descriptor: Does not mention open-source work.
Mentions occasional patches or lightweight contributions.
Shows regular contribution or some maintenance responsibility for a project.
Shows maintainer or roadmap-level responsibility for an actively used project with external contributors or a real community.

features.evidence: near-top finishes in several major events
features.name: offensive security practice
features.description: Captures active practice in adversarial thinking through capture-the-flag or similar offensive exercises.

levels.descriptor: Does not mention offensive practice.
Mentions occasional or casual capture-the-flag participation.
Shows regular or serious capture-the-flag practice.
Shows unusually strong offensive engagement through near-top placements, major-event results, or very serious ongoing practice.

features.name: security certification strength
features.description: Scores the strength of explicit third-party security credentials cited.

levels.descriptor: Mentions no security certification.
Mentions a baseline credential such as Security+ or a comparable fundamentals certification.
Mentions a demanding hands-on credential such as OSCP or an equivalent offensive certification.

features.evidence: distributed job scheduler with leader election and crash recovery
features.name: personal project ambition
features.description: Assesses whether side projects signal extra engineering depth and how technically ambitious they are.

levels.descriptor: Does not mention any personal project.
Mentions a small utility or hobby project with limited technical stretch.
Mentions a substantive self-directed project with some systems depth or clear engineering challenge.
Mentions an ambitious systems project tackling hard distributed, storage, consistency, or recovery problems.

features.evidence: favorite recent win was replacing a crumbling heuristic
features.name: concreteness of achievements
features.description: Captures how much the letter supports claims with specific achievements, mechanisms, or outcomes rather than broad adjectives.

levels.descriptor: Relies mostly on generic claims and role-alignment statements with no concrete example.
Includes some concrete nouns or responsibilities but little detail about what changed or why it mattered.
Includes at least one clear example with a technical mechanism, result, or before-and-after contrast.
Uses multiple specific examples that make the applicant's contributions and level of impact easy to picture.

features.name: narrative coherence
features.description: Assesses whether the letter organizes experience into a convincing career arc toward this role instead of a loose list of qualifications.

levels.descriptor: Reads as a disconnected inventory of facts or a compliance-style form letter.
Has some stated motivation, but the link from prior work to this role is thin or mechanical.
Presents a coherent progression from prior experience to the target role.
Tells a memorable, well-shaped story that makes the move into this role feel natural, intentional, and earned.

features.evidence: the best outcome is that nothing happens
features.name: stylistic voice
features.description: Captures how memorable and distinctive the prose feels beyond raw correctness.

levels.descriptor: Mostly uses flat template language or closely echoes the posting without a personal voice.
Shows some personal wording but remains largely conventional and forgettable.
Uses several original turns of phrase or vivid sentences that give the letter personality.
Sustains a distinctive voice throughout and leaves a clear stylistic impression.

features.name: writing polish
features.description: Scores mechanical quality and professionalism of the prose, especially spelling, grammar, and sentence control.

levels.descriptor: Frequent spelling, grammar, or usage errors distract from the content and undermine credibility.
Noticeable but nonfatal errors or awkward constructions appear in several places.
Generally clean and readable, with only minor issues.
Polished, fluent, and effectively error-free.

features.evidence: someone always inherits what we build
features.name: maintainer mindset
features.description: Captures whether the letter signals respect for maintenance, operability, and long-lived systems rather than only feature delivery.

levels.descriptor: Does not signal any particular maintenance or operability orientation.
Briefly references reliability, testing, or keeping systems running.
Clearly emphasizes maintenance, inherited systems, or the responsibility of operating durable services.
Expresses a strong stewardship ethos, such as building for inheritance, quiet resilience, higher standards, or long-term operational trust.
